body:
A board step can now be launched from a read-only clone of the board: no add_repo, nothing typed in chat. The real run in Harmonize, and the matching edit to Harmonize's hand-over skill, are the orchestrator's (handoff).

## What changed
- `_launch_in_clone` (`scripts/kit.py`): the prompt is committed in the clone and pushed as before. When the push is refused **for access** ("not in this session's authorized repository set", permission denied, an HTTP 403, authentication failed...), the launch carries on: the clone's launch runs, then the create_session call is rewritten so its `prompt` reads "Your prompt follows; first commit it to docs/prompts/<post>.md on your branch (it could not be pushed to the board), then read it and do it." followed by the rest of the start message and the full text in a `<prompt path=...>` block. `source_url` stays the board, `source_revision` becomes the step's branch when origin already has it, else the trunk (the unpushed commit would not clone), `outcome_branch` is unchanged.
- The prompt commit is taken back out of the clone afterwards, and after any failed push, so the clone never holds a commit origin lacks.
- A push that fails for another reason (network) still stops the launch with the error, as before. A push that works keeps the old path.
- `launch_text` says so in one line. `resume --role orchestrator` (launch step 3), the no-clone message and lesson K1 now say: clone the public board read-only, nothing to attach.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[kit.py launch post] --> B[commit prompt in board clone]
  B --> C{push}
  C -->|ok| D[create_session: Your prompt is path]
  C -->|refused for access| E[create_session: prompt text inline, source_revision trunk]
  C -->|other error| F[error, as before]
  E --> G[drop the local prompt commit]
```

## Tests
- `tests/test_cl40_launch_readonly.py`: a bare remote with a pre-receive hook that refuses with the O57 message. 6 of 6 pass; with the old `scripts/kit.py` 4 fail.
- Full suite: 11 of 11 suites passed, 0 failed.

## The orchestrator's gaps (O57), fixed
1. Notes under CL38/CL39: comments `cl40-note-cl38` and `cl40-note-cl39` (on the Artifact since 04:36).
2. `source_revision` is `origin/<branch>` when the step's branch exists there, else the trunk.
3. The denial match no longer takes any "403": only `returned error: 403`, `HTTP 403`, `status 403`, `403 Forbidden`.
4. A failed push (any reason) resets the prompt commit: with `trunk_push`, main stays where origin has it.

## Notes under CL38 and CL39
A comment on each: the environment's repository list and add_repo at turn 1 are not needed to launch a board step. Still useful: the doctor's add_repo warning and `kit.py attach` for a session where the owner types, and the user-level hooks (`.kit/user_hooks.py`) for a session started outside a repo.

## Not done here
Harmonize's `orchestrator-handoff` skill and `_handover` live in anlonlt/harmonize, which a part never attaches: the orchestrator drops their add_repo step (handoff).
handoff: Orchestrator: (1) in Harmonize, `install.py --update` so .kit/kit.py has CL40; then, from a read-only clone of anlonlt/board next to it, `kit.py launch <a board post>`: expect 'The prompt could not be pushed to the board' and a create_session whose prompt holds the text; write it in real_project. (2) In Harmonize, drop the add_repo step from the orchestrator-handoff skill and _handover: clone the board read-only (public, `git clone https://github.com/anlonlt/board ../board`), launches go through this path. Commands checked: kit.py commands launch/attach, _launch_attached, _prompt_branch, launch_text, web-env.

title: Launch a board step without push access to the board (prompt carried in the start message)
verdict: kit.py launch now starts a board step from a read-only clone: when the prompt push is refused for access, the create_session prompt carries the prompt's full text and the session commits it first.
